title: Vote share cutoff and policy adoption

llm_response.content:
## 1. Identification Strategy
To address the research question of whether winning a ballot initiative (vote share ≥ 50%) causes a discontinuous jump in municipal spending on the targeted policy, we will employ a Sharp Regression Discontinuity Design (RDD). The key assumption in this design is that the vote share threshold (50%) is the only factor determining policy adoption at the cutoff point, and the continuity of the underlying distribution of potential outcomes. By comparing the municipal spending changes just above and just below the 50% threshold, we can identify the causal effect of winning the ballot initiative on municipal spending.

## 2. R Code
```r
# Load necessary libraries
library(readr)
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)

# Read the data
data <- read_csv("experiments/exp_b/data/s25_data.csv")

# Fit the sharp RDD model
# We'll use a simple linear model for the treated and control groups separately
# around the cutoff (0.5) for observations near the cutoff (|running_var - 0.5| <= 0.3)

# Filter observations near the cutoff
data_near_cutoff <- data %>% filter(near_cutoff == 1)

# Run the regression for observations near the cutoff
# First, for treated (running_var >= 0.5)
treated_model <- lm(y ~ running_var, data = data_near_cutoff %>% filter(treated == 1))
# Second, for control (running_var < 0.5)
control_model <- lm(y ~ running_var, data = data_near_cutoff %>% filter(treated == 0))

# Predict y at the cutoff for both groups
# Treated group prediction at the cutoff
treated_pred <- predict(treated_model, newdata = data.frame(running_var = 0.5))
# Control group prediction at the cutoff
control_pred <- predict(control_model, newdata = data.frame(running_var = 0.5))

# Calculate the discontinuity (the treatment effect)
discontinuity <- treated_pred - control_pred
print(paste("The estimated treatment effect (discontinuity) is:", discontinuity))

# For robustness, also include a pooled regression with interaction term
pooled_model <- lm(y ~ running_var + treated + running_var:treated, data = data_near_cutoff)
summary(pooled_model)

# Plot the data and regression lines for visualization
ggplot(data_near_cutoff, aes(x = running_var, y = y, color = factor(treated))) +
  geom_point() +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = FALSE) +
  labs(title = "RDD Plot", x = "Vote Share", y = "Log Municipal Spending Change")
```

## 3. Expected Findings
Given the nature of the research question, we expect a positive discontinuity (jump) in municipal spending on the targeted policy at the 50% vote share threshold. This is because winning a ballot initiative is expected to lead to an increase in municipal spending on the policy in question, as the initiative's passage directly influences budget allocations. The magnitude of the discontinuity will depend on various factors, including the specific nature of the policy, the size of the jurisdiction, and the political context. However, we anticipate the effect to be statistically significant, indicating a clear causal relationship between winning a ballot initiative and the subsequent increase in municipal spending. The exact magnitude (e.g., a 10% increase in spending) will depend on the data analysis results.

_ground_truth.identification_strategy: Sharp RDD — cutoff = 50% vote share; local linear regression with optimal bandwidth
_ground_truth.conclusion_detail: Passing the initiative causes a discrete jump in targeted spending
